text:
sam: Customer on dedicated pool 'dedicated-rua-acme' reporting intermittent 429s + p99 latency spikes during their hourly ETL burst. They say this started after last week's rollout. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-support/acme/2026-03-09/trace.log — asking if anyone changed reserved-pool or token-bucket defaults.
jordan: Do we have the request/response headers (x-rate-limit*, x-reserved-pool-*) from the failed calls? Need to know if they hit their reserved pool or fell back to global.
sam: Quick sample from their headers: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-reserved-pool-available: 0`, `x-pool-throughput-cap: 1200`. They saw ~8k requests in a 30s window, then lots of 429s. No auth failures.
maria: I remember a runtime tweak recently — we reduced max burst/default token bucket sizes for dedciated pools to control tail GPU oversubscription. That could reduce headroom for short bursts. PR reference looks like runtime#412.
jordan: Eng-runtime, can you surface metrics: `reservedpool.available_tokens`, `token_bucket.capacity`, and `pool.tokens.refill_rate` for dedicated-rua-acme around the incident window? Also any config change timestamps.
eng-runtime-bot: Snapshot (10m window around 2026-03-09T02:10Z): `reservedpool.available_tokens`: 0 -> 3, `token_bucket.capacity`: 300 (was 1500 before 2026-03-06T18:12Z), `pool.tokens.refill_rate`: 40r/s. Config change: `dedicated.token_bucket.max_burst` set to `300` in rollout `runtime/2026-03-06`.
sam: That aligns with customer's timeline. They expect their dedicated SLA (p95/p99 headroom) — reducing bucket to 300 would cause short bursts to exhaust tokens quickly.
maria: Agreed. Action proposal: 1) Temporary rollback/increase max_burst for this customer's pool back to 1500 to absorb their ETL spikes; 2) Add a per-customer `safety_margin` config so reserved pools keep X% headroom for known batch windows; 3) Notify CS and schedule follow-up postmortem. Thoughts?
jordan: +1. I'll coordinate the rollback window and monitor queues/underprovision. Also add extra tracing for failed requests (capture x-request-id). Sam, ask customer for a compact repro script/timestamps so we can validate post-change. Example spike script: ``for i in {1..8000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' & done``
sam: Pinged customer for the exact token and timing. They gave a sample window: 2026-03-09T02:09:30Z - 02:10:05Z.
ops_bot: Scheduling a config change: applying `dedicated.token_bucket.max_burst=1500` to pool `dedicated-rua-acme` in 10 minutes. Will monitor `reservedpool.available_tokens` and error rate for 30m post-change and report back. :hammer_and_wrench:
maria: If rollback reduces 429s and restores p95, we should log this as a regression from the runtime change and add an override knob for high-throughput customers. Also review cost tradeoffs (higher burst may increase short-term GPU spin-up).
jordan: I'll watch the metrics and collect a before/after diff. Sam, once we confirm, please coordinate the customer's billing/contact so they see resolution.
sam: Will do. Thanks team — will update thread after ops_bot report and customer repro run. :thumbsup:
